 JUDGMENT Heard learned counsel Sri. M.K.Soudaghar and Sri.Deepak Maganur.

2. KSRTC has filed the appeal challenging the validity of the judgment and award passed in MVC No.22/2018 dated 10.07.2019 on the file of Civil Judge Senior Division MACT Ron.
3.

sentences.text:
The undisputed facts are that the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-26/W-3161 lost his life involving the bus bearing No.KA-26/F-817 in a road traffic accident that occurred on 18.04.2017 at about 5 p.m.
4.
Wife of the deceased and son of the deceased have filed the claim petition.

Same was resisted and learned trial judge on recording the evidence of the parties assessed the compensation in a sum of Rs.11,92,571/- as under:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:727 Sl.No. Name of heads Amount(Rs.) 1 Loss of dependency 11,17,571-00 2 Loss of consortium 40,000-00 3 Loss of estate 15,000-00 4 Funeral expenses 15,000-00 5 Transportation of dead body 5,000-00 Total 11,92,571-00 5.

Learned counsel Sri.M.K.Soudhaghar for KSRTC vehemently contended that the sketch that has been part of the charge sheet papers would go to show that the accident has occurred in the middle of the road and total width of the road is 15 feet.
6.

As such, even though the charge sheet filed by police is against the driver of the KSRTC bus, some amount of contributory negligence needs to be attributed to rider of the motorcycle and accordingly,
Divisional Controller vs Smt.Annapurna @ Annavva W/O. Kariyappa ... on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191031113/
2
attributing the contributory negligence to the extent of 25% would meet the ends of justice.

7. Insofar as the quantum of compensation is concerned Sri.Soudhaghar contended that second claimant NC: 2024:KHC-D:727 is gainfully employed and is earning money as a coolie and therefore, he could not be treated as dependent and therefore, deducting 1/3 of the income, is incorrect and 50% would have been deducted by the tribunal while assessing the compensation.
8. Therefore, he has sought for reduction of the compensation.
9. Per contra, Sri.Deepak Maganur supported the impugned judgment and contended that no contributory negligence can be attributed to the rider of the motorcycle.

10. He also contended that in fact contended that on the head of loss of consortium, claimants are entitled for another sum of Rs.40,000/- by following the dictum of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and Others reported in AIR 2020 SC 3076 and Magma General Insurance Company NC: 2024:KHC-D:727 Limited vs. Nanu Ram and Others reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, and sought for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: 11. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this court has perused the material on record meticulously.
12. On such perusal of the material on record, admittedly, charge sheet came to be filed against driver of the KSRTC bus.

However, there is some force in the argument put forth by KSRTC that some amount of contributory negligence ought to have been attributed to the rider of the motorcycle, looking into the sketch that has been part of the charge sheet material.
The sketch has been produced before the court along with memo by the appellant.
13. This court has perused the sketch.
As per sketch, the accident has occurred in the middle of the road.

14. Therefore, the tribunal ought to have been attributed some amount of contributory negligence to the rider of the NC: 2024:KHC-D:727 motorcycle while directing the compensation to be paid by the appellant.

15. Taking note of the fact that accident is of the year 2017, and the deceased was a post man, the assessment of the compensation in the considered opinion of this court is just and proper even though the tribunal has granted only sum of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium.

16. Accordingly, attributing the contributory negligence to an extent of 10% to the rider of the motorcycle would meets the ends of justice taking note of the complaint averments and also the fact that the charge sheet came to be filed only against KSRTC bus driver.

17. Accordingly, the following :

3 ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.

ii) While maintaining the quantum of compensation in a sum of Rs.11,92,571/-, 10%
of contributory negligence is to be attributed to NC: 2024:KHC-D:727 the rider of the motorcycle and therefore, the KSRTC is directed to pay 90% of sum of Rs.11,92,571/-
with interest at 8% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
iii) Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to the tribunal and balance amount to be deposited by the KSRTC within a period of 4 weeks from today.
